content.comment_body: I'm working on an application where I need message texts to indicate system status, such as ON or OFF. Currently, I use messages like "The heating system is ON" or "The heating system is OFF" by activating the corresponding text, which works but uses up two fields per system. Since there are only 10 message texts available on the [product_name], I can only show statuses for up to 5 systems. Is there a way to have message texts change dynamically, similar to how analogue values are handled, but using words for digital statuses like ON and OFF?

Since you only have 10 text fields, you're limited to showing ON/OFF for a maximum of 5 items. If you can wait a few weeks, there is a new [product_name] coming soon with 50 text fields, so you will be able to display statuses for up to 25 I/O items.
Hello, Take a look here: New [product_name] and [product_name] text display released for delivery. Best regards, [user_name]

Hello, The latest [product_name] also supports "status text," which does exactly what you're looking for. You can set up a message where part of the text changes depending on the input status, for example, displaying ON or OFF. This feature is available for the display on the new [product_name] and also for the [product_name] operator device. Hope this helps. Regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are seeking ways to display dynamic message texts indicating digital statuses (such as ON/OFF) within system messages on their controller, but are limited by hardware that only supports a small number of static fields. There is demand for greater flexibility and scalability in managing digital input status messages, similar to the handling of analogue values. Upcoming hardware versions promise to expand message capacity and introduce dynamic status text features for digital values.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the message text feature to allow dynamic substitution that reflects digital statuses (ON/OFF) within a single field, enabling easier scaling to show the status of many systems without doubling the number of required fields.
